answer: Agent identity derives from a slow-grown quartz-like rootstock: each agent must accumulate a long, publicly verifiable history of field trials before gaining full voting weight. Like grafting onto a hardy lotus, new agents borrow credibility only from a named sponsor whose own rootstock is slashed if the graft fails, so fake sybils inherit real liability. The cost is that an attacker must invest real seasons of work or corrupt an established willow-rooted sponsor, whose stake is forfeited on detection, though colluding sponsors remain the limit.
